an6.44:4.1: “This is what I did, venerable sir: in the morning I robed up and, taking my bowl and robe, went to the home of the laywoman Migasālā; arriving there, I sat down on the seat spread out.
an6.44:4.2: Then, venerable sir, the laywoman Migasālā came up to me; arriving at me, she bowed to me and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, venerable sir, the laywoman Migasālā said this to me:
an6.44:4.3: “Honorable Ānanda, how on earth are we supposed to understand the teaching taught by the Buddha, when the chaste and the unchaste are both reborn in exactly the same place in the next life.
an6.44:4.4: My father Purāṇa was chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.
an6.44:4.5: When he passed away the Buddha declared that, since he was a once-returner, he was reborn in the host of joyful gods.
an6.44:4.6: But my uncle Isidatta was not chaste; he lived content with his wife.
an6.44:4.7: When he passed away the Buddha declared that, since he too was a once-returner, he was reborn in the host of joyful gods.
an6.44:4.8: How on earth are we supposed to understand the teaching taught by the Buddha, when the chaste and the unchaste are both reborn in exactly the same place in the next life?”
an6.44:4.9: Having said that, I addressed the laywoman Migasālā like this:
an6.44:4.10: ‘Yes, sister, but that’s how the Buddha declared it.’”
